title: OpalRun private deployment - daily implementation scratch
content:
Status snapshot (quick):
- OpalRun PoC env up in VPC (basic networking validated) — E2E pipeline still flaky for autoscaling events.
- Have a dedicated pool request approved (2 x A100 equivalent reserved) for initial week of load testing (billing owner: finance-contact@opalrun.com).
- Customer wants 99.9% read availability and 90th percentile generation latency < 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens).

Open questions / blockers:
- Can we get TLS client cert rotation documented for their KMS setup? KMS owner asked for HSM key policy details. (need SSO/KMS diagram)
- Autoscaler: tuned policy triggers too aggressively; causes node churn on MLFLOW tests. Need safe defaults for dedicated pools.
- When falling back to CPU quantized variant, what's expected degradation? Ops wants a sample latency table for routing policy decision.

Daily todo (03/08):
- [ ] Run load test with seq len distribution: 60% short (<=128), 30% mid (129-512), 10% long (512+). Script: load/test_opalrun.sh (local) -> upload results to Confluence page.
- [ ] Re-run kernel-selection experiment with --kv-prefetch enabled; compare token/s throughput. Use bench harness: infra/bench/serve-bench --model redwood-7b-q4f --batching auto --kv-prefetch true. Log outputs.
- [ ] Draft autoscaling playbook for dedicated pool: add hysteresis 90s, min-instances 2, scale-step 1, probe-window 60s. Push to PR 887 for review.
- [ ] Confirm route priority: prefer dedicated-us-west -> hosted-fallback -> private-region-eu as emergency fallback. Share with customer for approval.

Notes from yesterday's call w/ OpalRun (02/28):
- They will run heavy retraining cadence every Fri night — we must ensure KV cache warmup after deploys. Action: pre-warm KV cache using replay tool (tools/cache-warm.py) starting at 0200 UTC on Fridays.
- Compliance: they asked for audit log retention of 13 months. Need retention cost estimate from finance.

Quick config snippets (copyable):
- rollout policy: 
  - canary: 10% traffic for 1 hour -> if error_rate < 0.5% then increase 50% -> full after 6h
  - fallback: model_variant: redwood-7b-q4f-cpu (cpu-quant)

- example routing policy (YAML):
  routing_priority:
    - type: dedicated_pool
      region: us-west1
      pool_name: opalrun-dedicated-1
    - type: hosted_api
      region: global
    - type: private_region
      region: eu-west1
      pool_name: opalrun-private-backup

Implementation hints / gotchas: 
- KV caching: make sure prefix caching is enabled for session-type 'short-completion' else warmup will be ineffective.
- Quantization: for redwood-7b-q4f we observed 12-18% quality delta on instruction-following tests vs fp16 for some prompts — include those prompts in eval set before enabling CPU fallback.
- Batching: automatic batching gives best avg cost but watch P95 latency; for their SLO we might need explicit max_batch_size=8 for generation endpoints.

Customer-specific folder mapping (local to their repo):
- infra/deploy/opalrun/vpc.tf (network + peering)
- infra/serve/opalrun/pool-config.yaml (pool definitions + autoscale rules)
- infra/ops/runbooks/opalrun-warmup.md

Conversation snippets (notes to self):
- "If we can't meet 350ms at 90th with 7b on A100, propose a 13b optimized variant with lower quantization aggressive settings." 
- "Maya said they'll try a smaller prompt template to keep token counts down; coordinate for A/B test on Wednesday."

Quick commands to run (local):
- ssh jump -> gcloud compute ssh opalrun-runner --zone=us-west1-b
- ./tools/cache-warm.py --model redwood-7b-q4f --session-file sessions/opalrun-seed.json --parallel 4
- infra/bench/serve-bench --target http://opalrun-private:8080 --duration 10m --qps 120 --seq-dist 60,30,10

PRs / tickets to follow up:
- OPR-412: dedicated pool provisioning (status: in progress, assignee: Liam)
- OPR-419: audit log retention & KMS policy (status: needs info, assignee: Maya)
- PR 887: autoscale defaults (needs SRE review)

Metrics to collect during next run:
- 50th, 90th, 95th latency for generation (split by seq len bins)
- token/s throughput and tokens billed (compare to hosted baseline)
- cold-start penalty after deploy (measure first 10 requests into new node)
- error rate by model variant and route

Retention / handoff notes (for next SE or CSM):
- customer primary: ops-lead@opalrun.com (preferred Slack: direct, timezone: PST)
- CSM: Priya Rao (intro on Friday retrospective)
- Deliverable before next sync (03/12): latency whitepaper with 2 load profiles + recommended pool sizing, plus cost delta table (hosted vs dedicated).

Random scratch (ideas / future):
- Try tiny-intermediate cache tier (memcached close to app) to reduce cold-starts for repeated short prompts.
- Explore dynamic quantization profile that picks q4f for low-latency short prompts and q5b for long context to preserve quality.

End of jot.

-- S.M.
